sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: In September 1958, Bank of America decided to try an experiment,
sentences.zh: 1958年9月，美国银行决定进行一项实验，

sentences.en: one that would have far-reaching effects on our lives and on the economy.
sentences.zh: 这项实验将对我们的生活和经济产生深远的影响。

sentences.en: They decided, after careful consideration, to conduct this experiment in Fresno, California.
sentences.zh: 经过慎重考虑，他们决定在加利福尼亚州的弗雷斯诺进行这项实验。

sentences.en: The thinking was, no one was paying much attention to Fresno,
sentences.zh: 他们的想法是，当时没人太关注弗雷斯诺，

sentences.en: so if the plan failed, it wouldn't get a lot of media attention.
sentences.zh: 所以如果计划失败，也不会引起太多的媒体关注。

sentences.en: Things were slow back then here.
sentences.zh: 那时候这里的生活节奏很慢。

sentences.en: Fresno was not the big metropolitan area it is today.
sentences.zh: 弗雷斯诺当时还不是今天这样的大都市区。

sentences.en: That's Joseph Rusak.
sentences.zh: 那是约瑟夫·鲁萨克。

sentences.en: My name is Joseph Rusak.
sentences.zh: 我叫约瑟夫·鲁萨克。

sentences.en: I've worked with Bank of America since 1956 and retired in 1985.
sentences.zh: 我从1956年开始在美国银行工作，1985年退休。

sentences.en: Started off as a teller and worked our way up, as most of us young fellows did.
sentences.zh: 像我们大多数年轻人一样，我从柜员做起，一步步晋升。

sentences.en: Joseph was there when all of this went down.
sentences.zh: 这一切发生时，约瑟夫就在现场。

sentences.en: And so, in September of 1958, Bank of America sent out 60,000 pieces of mail to people in Fresno,
sentences.zh: 因此，在1958年9月，美国银行向弗雷斯诺的居民寄出了6万封邮件，

sentences.en: inside, with a little plastic object that has become in equal parts
sentences.zh: 里面装着一个小塑料物件，它后来成为了

sentences.en: emblematic of opportunity, convenience, and debt.
sentences.zh: 机遇、便利和债务的象征。

sentences.en: He's talking about the credit card.
sentences.zh: 他指的是信用卡。

sentences.en: That's reporter Nate Berg, here to tell you what I'm talking about.
sentences.zh: 那是记者内特·伯格，他来告诉你我所说的是什么。

sentences.en: Bank of America had recruited about 300 merchants in Fresno to accept this new payment system.
sentences.zh: 美国银行在弗雷斯诺招募了大约300家商户来接受这种新的支付系统。

sentences.en: And they'd asked employees like Joseph to hand credit cards out to people they knew.
sentences.zh: 他们还要求像约瑟夫这样的员工把信用卡发给他们认识的人。

sentences.en: We did.
sentences.zh: 我们确实照做了。

sentences.en: We'd pass it around to our friends and, you know, the neighbors, and that's about it.
sentences.zh: 我们会把它分发给朋友和邻居，差不多就是这样。

sentences.en: But as for Joseph, he was skeptical about using a credit card himself.
sentences.zh: 但至于约瑟夫本人，他对使用信用卡持怀疑态度。

sentences.en: To be honest with you, I don't remember if I took a card right, better or not, or if I waited a couple years.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我不记得我当时是否真的领了卡，或者是否等了几年才用。

sentences.en: But as a banker, I didn't really believe in credit myself.
sentences.zh: 但作为一名银行职员，我本人并不真正相信信贷。

sentences.en: Why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: Well, you have to pay back interest, and I don't like giving money away.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你得支付利息，而我不喜欢把钱白白送人。

sentences.en: Joseph wasn't alone.
sentences.zh: 约瑟夫并非个例。

sentences.en: The whole town of Fresno was a bit nervous about this new credit card system.
sentences.zh: 整个弗雷斯诺镇对这种新的信用卡系统都感到有些不安。

sentences.en: The concept of credit wasn't new, but it had never been done quite like this.
sentences.zh: 信贷的概念并不新鲜，但从未以这种方式实施过。

sentences.en: Going back into, say, the 1800s, early 1900s, you had credit with a store or some kind of a business.
sentences.zh: 追溯到19世纪或20世纪初，你可以在商店或某种企业里赊账。

sentences.en: It was just kind of a ledger book type of thing.
sentences.zh: 那只是一种记账本之类的东西。

sentences.en: This is Ken Hallenbeck.
sentences.zh: 这位是肯·哈伦贝克。

sentences.en: He's a numismatiSt.
sentences.zh: 他是一位钱币学家。

sentences.en: A numismatiSt.
sentences.zh: 钱币学家。

sentences.en: That is, someone who studies or collects currency.
sentences.zh: 也就是研究或收藏货币的人。

sentences.en: Not just coins, but it's paper money, medals, tokens, anything that's a money or a money substitute.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是硬币，还包括纸币、奖章、代币，任何货币或货币替代品。

sentences.en: Ken is retired now, but he used to work at the American Numismatic Association.
sentences.zh: 肯现在已经退休了，但他过去在美国钱币协会工作。

sentences.en: New-mis-matic.
sentences.zh: 钱币学家。

sentences.en: So, back in the late 1800s, every place from the corner bar to the local pharmacy allowed patrons to keep open tabs.
sentences.zh: 在19世纪末，从街角的酒吧到当地的药店，每个地方都允许顾客挂账。

sentences.en: They'd record everything in a ledger book and allow their customers to charge up a bill that they'd typically pay back at the end of the month.
sentences.zh: 他们会把一切记录在账本上，让顾客记账消费，通常在月底结清。

sentences.en: For businesses, this was an accounting nightmare.
sentences.zh: 对于企业来说，这是一场会计噩梦。

sentences.en: Stores could have hundreds of accounts, billing tabs for a dollar here and a dollar there.
sentences.zh: 商店可能有数百个账户，这里记一美元，那里记一美元。

sentences.en: And with each charge, a shopkeeper would have to haul out a ledger book and look up a customer's records just to complete a transaction.
sentences.zh: 每发生一笔消费，店主就得搬出账本，查阅顾客的记录才能完成交易。

sentences.en: Eventually, store owners cut down on some of the paperwork by assigning customers account numbers, which they would inscribe on little tokens.
sentences.zh: 最终，店主们通过给顾客分配账号并刻在小代币上来减少文书工作。

sentences.en: Most of them were round or oval, a hole in them, and they had a number on them, and that was your account number.
sentences.zh: 它们大多是圆形或椭圆形的，上面有个孔，刻着数字，那就是你的账号。

sentences.en: Ken has a collection of a few dozen of these old credit tokens, many dating back to the early 20th century.
sentences.zh: 肯收藏了几十个这种旧的信贷代币，许多可以追溯到20世纪初。

sentences.en: I have one here.
sentences.zh: 我这里就有一个。

sentences.en: It says Pocahontas Pioneer Garage, but it has a head of an Indian on it.
sentences.zh: 上面写着“波卡洪塔斯先锋车库”，但上面印着一个印第安人的头像。

sentences.en: And on the back, it has a number 839.
sentences.zh: 背面印着数字839。

sentences.en: After credit tokens came something called charge-a-plates.
sentences.zh: 在信贷代币之后，出现了一种叫做“Charge-a-Plate”的金属板。

sentences.en: They looked like little dog tags for the army.
sentences.zh: 它们看起来像军队的狗牌。

sentences.en: They were metal and had your name and information imprinted on them.
sentences.zh: 它们是金属做的，上面印有你的姓名和信息。

sentences.en: Shopkeepers could make an impression of your personal information directly onto the bill, instead of having to write it all down.
sentences.zh: 店主可以直接把你的个人信息压印在账单上，而不必手写。

sentences.en: But the more accounts you had, the more charge-a-plates and tokens you had to carry around with you.
sentences.zh: 但你拥有的账户越多，随身携带的金属板和代币就越多。

sentences.en: It still wasn't a great system for the retailer or the customer.
sentences.zh: 这对零售商或顾客来说仍然不是一个好的系统。

sentences.en: So, in 1949, a New York businessman named Frank X.
sentences.zh: 因此，在1949年，一位名叫弗兰克·X·麦克纳马拉的纽约商人

sentences.en: McNamara came up with an idea for a single charge card that could be accepted at multiple establishments.
sentences.zh: 提出了一个想法：一张可以在多家机构通用的单一签账卡。

sentences.en: He called it the diner's club card.
sentences.zh: 他称之为“大来卡”。

sentences.en: And with it, you could make charges at a number of New York restaurants and hotels.
sentences.zh: 有了它，你可以在纽约的许多餐厅和酒店消费。

sentences.en: But unlike the credit card of today, you could only use your diner's club card in certain places.
sentences.zh: 但与今天的信用卡不同，你只能在特定的地方使用大来卡。

sentences.en: The idea caught on somewhat.
sentences.zh: 这个想法在一定程度上流行了起来。

sentences.en: About 20,000 people signed up, mostly businessmen.
sentences.zh: 大约有2万人注册，主要是商人。

sentences.en: It wasn't a smash success.
sentences.zh: 它并没有取得巨大的成功。

sentences.en: But still, the banks started to see an opportunity.
sentences.zh: 但银行开始看到了机会。

sentences.en: So, you have this giant change taking place right around World War II, and especially in the aftermath of World War II,
sentences.zh: 二战前后，尤其是二战结束后，发生了巨大的变化，

sentences.en: when the American economy was basically the only economy in the world that was still standing.
sentences.zh: 当时美国经济基本上是世界上唯一屹立不倒的经济体。

sentences.en: That's Joe Nocera, columnist for the New York Times and author of A Piece of the Action, How the Middle Class Joined the Money Class.
sentences.zh: 那是乔·诺塞拉，《纽约时报》专栏作家，《行动的一份子：中产阶级如何加入金钱阶层》一书的作者。

sentences.en: People, having gotten through the war, settling down, you know, getting married, raising kids, wanting to live in the suburbs,
sentences.zh: 人们经历了战争，安定下来，结婚、养育孩子、想要住在郊区，

sentences.en: there were suddenly things they wanted to buy.
sentences.zh: 突然间有了他们想买的东西。

sentences.en: A refrigerator, for example.
sentences.zh: 比如冰箱。

sentences.en: Or, as it came into vogue, a television.
sentences.zh: 或者，随着流行起来的电视机。

sentences.en: So, maybe you'd have a Sears account.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可能有一个西尔斯百货的账户。

sentences.en: You could buy things there and pay your bill at the end of the month.
sentences.zh: 你可以在那里买东西，月底付账。

sentences.en: But if you didn't have an account with a store, you'd have to go to a bank and get a traditional loan for any relatively large purchase.
sentences.zh: 但如果你在某家店没有账户，你就得去银行申请传统贷款来购买任何相对昂贵的商品。

sentences.en: Whether it was a car, whether it was a sofa, whether it was a refrigerator, you'd go to the bank every single time.
sentences.zh: 无论是买车、买沙发还是买冰箱，你每次都得去银行。

sentences.en: Every single time, you know, you had to, you know, have collateral to pay for it.
sentences.zh: 每次，你都得有抵押品来支付。

sentences.en: Every single time, the banker would have to figure out whether you were a good credit risk.
sentences.zh: 每次，银行职员都得评估你是否具备良好的信贷风险。

sentences.en: It was a pretty cumbersome process, both for the consumer and for the bank.
sentences.zh: 这对消费者和银行来说都是一个相当繁琐的过程。

sentences.en: Bank of America wanted to find an easier way to make these small loans.
sentences.zh: 美国银行想找到一种更简单的方法来发放这些小额贷款。

sentences.en: Bank of America was, in the 1950s, the premier consumer-oriented bank in the United States.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪50年代，美国银行是美国首屈一指的面向消费者的银行。

sentences.en: Bank of America really believed in the idea that it would grow by helping consumers.
sentences.zh: 美国银行坚信通过帮助消费者来实现自身增长的理念。

sentences.en: So, it was Bank of America that decided that they would basically give clients a card that they could put in their pockets
sentences.zh: 因此，美国银行决定给客户一张可以放在口袋里的卡，

sentences.en: that would give them roughly a $500 line of credit.
sentences.zh: 给他们大约500美元的信用额度。

sentences.en: Unlike the Diners Club, Bank of America wanted their customers to be able to use their card anywhere, not just at restaurants.
sentences.zh: 与大来卡不同，美国银行希望客户能在任何地方使用他们的卡，而不仅仅是在餐厅。

sentences.en: And where the Diners Club had to be paid off within 60 days, Bank of America would allow its customers to pay them back whenever they wanted.
sentences.zh: 而且大来卡必须在60天内还清，而美国银行允许客户随时还款。

sentences.en: They'd call their new credit card the Bank AmeriCard.
sentences.zh: 他们把这种新信用卡称为“美洲银行卡”。

sentences.en: You could spend it all down, you could pay part of it back, you could pay it all back.
sentences.zh: 你可以花光额度，可以还一部分，也可以全部还清。

sentences.en: You didn't have to get a banker to approve your purchase, and you didn't have to pay the bank back by any specific time.
sentences.zh: 你不需要银行职员批准你的购买，也不需要在特定时间内还款。

sentences.en: They called this revolving credit.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为循环信贷。

sentences.en: The card was essentially an instant loan.
sentences.zh: 这张卡本质上是一笔即时贷款。

sentences.en: Of course, it was a loan with an interest rate attached.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是一笔附带利息的贷款。

sentences.en: This was one of the profound shifts in the way people handle money.
sentences.zh: 这是人们处理金钱方式上的深刻转变之一。

sentences.en: Instead of the banker being in control of your money, of setting the terms for how you dealt with your money,
sentences.zh: 以前是银行职员控制你的钱，设定你处理金钱的条款，

sentences.en: with a credit card, you were the one setting the terms, and you were the one making the decisions about what to do with your money.
sentences.zh: 而有了信用卡，你才是设定条款的人，也是决定如何使用金钱的人。

sentences.en: Now, all Bank of America had to do was convince retailers to accept credit cards as payment and convince people to use them.
sentences.zh: 现在，美国银行所要做的就是说服零售商接受信用卡支付，并说服人们使用它们。

sentences.en: Now, because they were a new invention, and because people didn't really know what they were,
sentences.zh: 由于这是一种新发明，人们并不真正了解它是什么，

sentences.en: and because there were no laws surrounding credit cards,
sentences.zh: 而且当时没有任何关于信用卡的法律，

sentences.en: the way they tested the card was they simply sent a mailing to basically every Bank of America customer in Fresno, California.
sentences.zh: 他们测试这张卡的方法很简单：直接给加州弗雷斯诺的每一位美国银行客户寄了一封邮件。

sentences.en: Which brings us back to Fresno.
sentences.zh: 这又把我们带回了弗雷斯诺。

sentences.en: They called it the Fresno Drop.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为“弗雷斯诺投放”。

sentences.en: Bank of America mailed out 60,000 credit cards all over the city.
sentences.zh: 美国银行在全城寄出了6万张信用卡。

sentences.en: Fresno had become a laboratory for the future of personal finance.
sentences.zh: 弗雷斯诺成了个人理财未来的实验室。

sentences.en: The Fresno Drop was supposed to be a controlled experiment,
sentences.zh: “弗雷斯诺投放”本应是一项受控实验，

sentences.en: where the bank could test the concept and work out any kinks.
sentences.zh: 银行可以在这里测试这个概念并解决任何问题。

sentences.en: But within just a few months of the Fresno credit card drop,
sentences.zh: 但在弗雷斯诺信用卡投放后的短短几个月内，

sentences.en: Bank of America got word that one of its competitors in California was planning a similar program.
sentences.zh: 美国银行收到消息，其在加州的一家竞争对手正在计划类似的计划。

sentences.en: So Bank of America quickly expanded.
sentences.zh: 于是美国银行迅速扩张。

sentences.en: Mass mailings went out in the Central Valley cities of Modesto and Bakersfield,
sentences.zh: 大规模的邮件被寄往中央谷地的莫德斯托和贝克斯菲尔德，

sentences.en: and then eventually to the state's bigger cities of Sacramento, San Francisco, and Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 最终扩展到该州更大的城市萨克拉门托、旧金山和洛杉矶。

sentences.en: Within 10 months of the Fresno drop, more than a million Bank of America cards had been mailed out across California.
sentences.zh: 在弗雷斯诺投放后的10个月内，超过一百万张美国银行卡已在加州各地寄出。

sentences.en: Once the cards had begun saturating the bigger cities, fraud and theft were rampant.
sentences.zh: 当信用卡开始在大城市普及后，欺诈和盗窃行为猖獗。

sentences.en: People would go around to mailboxes in the suburbs and steal cards on days when they knew the cards were being dropped.
sentences.zh: 人们会在郊区的邮箱周围转悠，在他们知道卡片会被投递的日子里偷走卡片。

sentences.en: The system was being abused, but the system was also randomly mailing out pre-approved credit cards
sentences.zh: 系统被滥用了，但系统也在随机寄出预先批准的信用卡，

sentences.en: that allowed anyone to buy up to $500 of whatever they wanted.
sentences.zh: 允许任何人购买价值高达500美元的任何东西。

sentences.en: You know, dead people were getting cards, dogs were getting cards.
sentences.zh: 你知道，死人收到了卡，狗也收到了卡。

sentences.en: It was just very, very willy-nilly.
sentences.zh: 这简直太随意了。

sentences.en: Despite these mass mailings, the cards didn't catch on right away.
sentences.zh: 尽管进行了大规模邮寄，但这些卡并没有立即流行起来。

sentences.en: It was hard to convince stores to accept them.
sentences.zh: 说服商店接受它们很困难。

sentences.en: They had to pay a percentage of the sale to the bank.
sentences.zh: 他们必须向银行支付销售额的一定比例作为手续费。

sentences.en: And it was hard to get customers to use them.
sentences.zh: 而且很难让顾客使用它们。

sentences.en: And when people did start using the cards, they didn't always pay the money back,
sentences.zh: 当人们开始使用这些卡时，他们并不总是还钱，

sentences.en: which was a bit of a surprise to Bank of America.
sentences.zh: 这对美国银行来说有点意外。

sentences.en: People had mostly been pretty good about paying back traditional loans.
sentences.zh: 人们在偿还传统贷款方面通常表现得相当好。

sentences.en: And what they forgot was, in those days when you made a loan,
sentences.zh: 而他们忘记的是，在那个年代，当你发放贷款时，

sentences.en: the customer looked the banker in the eye, and the banker looked the customer in the eye,
sentences.zh: 顾客会看着银行职员的眼睛，银行职员也会看着顾客的眼睛，

sentences.en: and they both had this kind of relationship.
sentences.zh: 他们之间有某种关系。

sentences.en: And the customer would not want to let the banker down.
sentences.zh: 顾客不想让银行职员失望。

sentences.en: Whereas with a credit card, it was an anonymous thing.
sentences.zh: 而信用卡则是一种匿名的事情。

sentences.en: And this anonymity meant one in four people weren't paying their credit card debts.
sentences.zh: 这种匿名性意味着四分之一的人没有偿还信用卡债务。

sentences.en: In 1959, about a year after Bank of America did their first mass mailing in Fresno,
sentences.zh: 1959年，也就是美国银行在弗雷斯诺进行首次大规模邮寄大约一年后，

sentences.en: they had mailed out more than two million Bank AmeriCards.
sentences.zh: 他们已经寄出了超过两百万张美洲银行卡。

sentences.en: But they hadn't made a single cent from their experiment.
sentences.zh: 但他们从实验中没赚到一分钱。

sentences.en: In fact, they lost about $20 million.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们损失了大约2000万美元。

sentences.en: And so the bank started making a few changes.
sentences.zh: 于是银行开始做出一些改变。

sentences.en: They really started to think about it differently.
sentences.zh: 他们开始以不同的方式思考这个问题。

sentences.en: Bank of America set up a collections department and an anti-fraud unit.
sentences.zh: 美国银行成立了催收部门和反欺诈部门。

sentences.en: People who weren't paying their bills had their cards revoked.
sentences.zh: 不还钱的人会被吊销信用卡。

sentences.en: And the government also started to regulate the credit card industry.
sentences.zh: 政府也开始监管信用卡行业。

sentences.en: In 1968, the Truth in Lending Act made it illegal to mail out credit cards to people who never asked for one.
sentences.zh: 1968年，《诚实信贷法》规定，向从未申请过的人寄送信用卡是非法的。

sentences.en: From that point onward, instead of getting a card in the mail,
sentences.zh: 从那时起，你收到的不再是直接寄来的卡，

sentences.en: you got instead a solicitation to apply for a card,
sentences.zh: 而是申请信用卡的邀请函，

sentences.en: which in one form or another exists to this day.
sentences.zh: 这种形式一直延续至今。

sentences.en: It wasn't until 1961, three years after the Fresno drop,
sentences.zh: 直到1961年，也就是弗雷斯诺投放三年后，

sentences.en: that Bank of America actually turned a profit on their crazy credit card experiment.
sentences.zh: 美国银行才真正从他们疯狂的信用卡实验中获利。

sentences.en: By 1968, they were making about $13 million a year.
sentences.zh: 到1968年，他们每年赚取约1300万美元。

sentences.en: The Bank of America system, which became a nationwide system,
sentences.zh: 美国银行系统后来演变成全国性系统，

sentences.en: eventually became known as Visa.
sentences.zh: 最终被称为Visa。

sentences.en: And the other cards that had competed with Bank of America,
sentences.zh: 而其他与美国银行竞争的信用卡，

sentences.en: they also consolidated and they became MasterCard.
sentences.zh: 它们也进行了合并，最终成为了万事达卡。

sentences.en: The major credit card companies now make lots and lots and lots of money every year,
sentences.zh: 如今，各大信用卡公司每年赚取着数不胜数的巨额利润，

sentences.en: which is great for them.
sentences.zh: 这对他们来说当然是好事。

sentences.en: Maybe not so great for the rest of us.
sentences.zh: 但对我们其他人来说，可能就不那么美妙了。

sentences.en: Today, over 70% of American adults have at least one credit card.
sentences.zh: 如今，超过70%的美国成年人至少拥有一张信用卡。

sentences.en: And the U.S.
sentences.zh: 而整个美国，

sentences.en: as a whole has about $900 billion in credit card debt.
sentences.zh: 背负的信用卡债务总额约为9000亿美元。

sentences.en: In 2009, more credit card reform was passed.
sentences.zh: 2009年，美国通过了更多的信用卡改革法案。

sentences.en: It prevents arbitrary interest hikes,
sentences.zh: 它防止了随意的利率上调，

sentences.en: stops credit card companies from specifically marketing to college kids,
sentences.zh: 禁止信用卡公司专门针对大学生进行营销，

sentences.en: prohibits certain types of abusive fees.
sentences.zh: 并禁止了某些类型的滥收费项目。

sentences.en: But a lot of people think more reform is needed.
sentences.zh: 但许多人认为还需要进一步改革。

sentences.en: The experiment in Fresno created a tool that made buying things much, much easier.
sentences.zh: 弗雷斯诺的实验创造了一种让购物变得极其简单的工具。

sentences.en: You no longer had to put on a suit and a tie and go to the bank for a loan
sentences.zh: 你不再需要每次想买点好东西时，

sentences.en: every time you wanted to get yourself something nice.
sentences.zh: 都得穿上西装打好领带去银行申请贷款。

sentences.en: The credit card facilitated an unprecedented amount of economic freedom for the middle class.
sentences.zh: 信用卡为中产阶级带来了前所未有的经济自由。

sentences.en: And that aspect was intentional, and maybe even noble.
sentences.zh: 这一初衷是有意为之的，甚至可以说是高尚的。

sentences.en: But it's important to keep in mind that first and foremost,
sentences.zh: 但必须记住的是，首先且最重要的一点是，

sentences.en: the credit card was designed to make money for banks.
sentences.zh: 信用卡的设计初衷就是为了让银行赚钱。

sentences.en: And everything about their design betrays that primary objective.
sentences.zh: 而它们设计的方方面面都暴露了这一核心目标。

sentences.en: Credit cards don't have to be complicated.
sentences.zh: 信用卡本不必如此复杂。

sentences.en: They don't have to trick you.
sentences.zh: 它们本不必去欺骗你。

sentences.en: But they do.
sentences.zh: 但它们确实这么做了。

sentences.en: Because they were designed that way.
sentences.zh: 因为它们就是这样被设计的。

sentences.zh: 每天都在不断增加
